me_d_midcoast.blurb: Midcoast covers the coast and inland country of Maine from the Topsham end up toward Rockland, a stretch of small peninsulas with small towns tucked between them. Climbable rock is scarce, and the little there is, short walls and the odd boulder, is generally regarded as poor. Nearly everything here is bouldering, with a plentiful supply of easy and moderate problems, a solid middle of V3 to V5, and a few hard ones near the top end; ice, top-rope, trad and sport are only a handful of spots. Lisbon Falls has a big glacial erratic below the dam that makes a good afternoon stop. Whiskeag Crag, The Basin, Dodge Point and Birch Point are the other names to look for.

sd_southern_black_hills.blurb: The Southern Black Hills climbing centers on the town of Custer, with Hill City as the other main gateway, and spreads across the triangle between Custer, Hill City and Keystone. Around Custer the rock is mostly granite, with routes from single pitches to multi-pitch lines, and some limestone cliffs lie farther west, away from town. Routes mix traditionally protected climbs with bolted ones that can be run-out. Bouldering makes up about two thirds of the climbing here, from V0 up to V11, with the weight in the V3 to V5 range, and sport is most of the rest, mostly 5.10 to 5.12 with a few moderates. Custer Bouldering, Lightning Creek, Laughing Water Creek and Flag Mountain are the biggest sub-areas.

ut_triassic.blurb: Triassic is a bouldering zone in central Utah, roughly a 20-minute drive from Joe's Valley, on wide open ground well away from anything. Every problem here is a boulder problem, with a broad spread from V0 to V11 that peaks around V4 to V7, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners. At Land of a Thousand Boulders, the largest and busiest part, the rock is mostly sandstone with a few conglomerate climbs, and there are plenty of V0 to V2 problems alongside harder classics. Other pockets include Andy's Wash, Eon Blue Zone, Golden Ladle and Petroglyph.

bc_shannon_falls.blurb: Shannon Falls is a cluster of crags beside the falls near Squamish, just south of the Chief. Trad climbing dominates, with a good number of sport routes and a modest set of boulder problems, and the routes run from about 5.6 to 5.12 with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. The left side has low-angle single and multi-pitch lines, while the right side is steeper and more vertical. The Zen Garden is a forested, steep trad crag known for cracks, with a stack of boulder problems at its base. The Papoose, Shannon Falls Wall, Shannon Springs Wall, AMO Wall and Gobsmacking Wall fill out the rest. Approaches to the walls are short.

nh_oak_mountain.blurb: Oak Mountain is a bouldering area in New Hampshire's Lakes Region, a companion to nearby Bayle Mountain, with large erratics scattered through the woods and an adventurous feel. Almost all of it is boulder problems, from V0 through V7, with the most in the V2 to V5 range and a good handful of harder ones; there are a few trad lines at Connor Pond Crag. The boulders spread over several sections: the Entrance Boulders, the east and south sides of the mountain, and the River Boulders.

il_chicago_area.blurb: Climbing around Chicago is mostly urban bouldering, split between natural boulders and city structures such as bridges and the buildings downtown. Almost all of it is easy to moderate bouldering, with a big supply of problems from V0 to V4 and only a few harder ones. Henry C. Palmisano Nature Park has boulders, and Steelworkers Park on the lakefront in South Chicago climbs a 30-foot historic ore wall, with roped routes graded 5.2 to 5.7 and bouldering on the lower third. Other sites include the Union Pacific Traverse, the Northwestern University boulders and the lakefront trail bridges. There is a little trad, top-rope, sport and ice besides.
